name: ThinkSQL
tagline: One developer's ISO-SQL relational server written in Delphi, with MVCC; open-sourced under GPL in 2012.
description: ThinkSQL is Greg Gaughan's cross-platform relational database server, written in Object Pascal (Delphi and Kylix) with the goal of following the ISO SQL standard closely: transactions, sub-selects, views, set operators, privileges and full referential constraints, on a multi-threaded server with multi-version concurrency control, hash indexes for joins, online backups and a statistical query optimizer. It shipped native ODBC, JDBC, dbExpress and Python DB-API drivers. Sold commercially in the early 2000s, with version 1.04 in 2004 and royalty-free redistribution licences, its server source was released on GitHub under the GPL on 1 January 2012 and has seen almost no changes since. It is a rare, readable example of a complete SQL engine built by one person.
statusNote: Source on GitHub (GPL) since 2012 with no development since 2018; the website remains as an archive. Firebird or PostgreSQL are maintained alternatives.
strengths: Close adherence to ISO SQL, including views, set operators and referential constraints
MVCC on a multi-threaded server with online backups
Readable Pascal codebase useful for learning how a full SQL server works
weaknesses: Essentially unmaintained since its 2012 source release
Delphi/Kylix toolchain is hard to build today
useCases: Studying a complete single-author SQL server
Maintaining older applications built on it
